bug_semantics: An authenticated bot author can store a rich-text link whose URL uses the javascript: scheme. The @typebot.io/js viewer rendered that author-controlled link into the DOM without validating its scheme—initially by assigning serialized content.html to SolidJS innerHTML and, after a 2023 refactor, by assigning the rich-text element URL directly to an anchor href. When a visitor clicks the link, the browser executes the payload in the embedding host page's origin, allowing theft of host-origin cookies, session tokens, and other accessible data; victim authentication is not required.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructable BIC is PR #194's sole member commit 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894. It created packages/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/TextBubble.tsx and introduced the unsafe sink innerHTML={props.content.html} for author-controlled serialized rich text, while the pre-existing builder toolbar already exposed LinkToolbarButton without a protocol allowlist. GitHub landed the same parent and identical tree as mainline carrier 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc. Commit e0a9824913237cb5340d262770e9e8290fbc4002 later replaced the stored-HTML sink with a recursive Plate renderer containing <a href={props.element.url as string}>, preserving rather than originating the missing-scheme-validation flaw; 765c4b2f8c1fd4ec610bc81b2547efbda65452ae was another refactor of that same unsafe href.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894 shows human author Baptiste Arnaud <contact@baptiste-arnaud.fr>, human committer Baptiste Arnaud <contact@baptiste-arnaud.fr>, subject ':alembic: Implement bot v2 MVP', body 'Closes #190', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/baptisteArno/typebot.io/security/advisories/GHSA-hqmv-v56g-4m47 identifies packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/plate/PlateBlock.tsx, explains that SolidJS leaves javascript: href values unchanged, gives the authenticated-author-to-clicking-visitor attack path, and records application versions <=3.15.2 as affected and 3.16.0 as patched; the assigned bundle records npm @typebot.io/js <0.10.1 as affected and 0.10.1 as first patched. `git log -L 29,36:packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/plate/PlateBlock.tsx` traced the pre-fix href through 765c4b2f8c1fd4ec610bc81b2547efbda65452ae and back to e0a9824913237cb5340d262770e9e8290fbc4002. `git show e0a9824 -- .../PlateBlock.tsx` showed that e0a created the direct href renderer while replacing an existing `innerHTML={props.content.html}` renderer, so it was a mechanism-preserving refactor rather than the root BIC. Following that legacy sink to packages/js found mainline commit 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc. The public PR #194 patch begins `From 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894`; the object is present locally. `git rev-parse 1a3869^{tree} 3487850^{tree}` returned the same tree 1c7360226886e227373c9affe2a374c1fbe7c750, and both commits have parent e55823e0112291a32886908fd4c63365275106e6, proving 3487850 is the sole direct PR member behind the recreated mainline carrier. `git show 3487850 -- packages/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/TextBubble.tsx` shows the new 69-line component and its unsanitized `innerHTML={props.content.html}` sink. `git show e55823e:apps/builder/.../TextBubbleEditor/ToolBar.tsx` shows the already-present `LinkToolbarButton`, while `git cat-file -e e55823e:packages/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/TextBubble.tsx` fails because the sink file is absent from the immediate parent. `git tag --contains 1a3869 --list 'js-v*' --sort=version:refname` starts at js-v0.0.1, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1a3869 js-v0.0.1` succeeds, placing the landed tree in the first @typebot.io/js release. At the upper boundary, `git diff js-v0.10.0 js-v0.10.1 -- .../PlateBlock.tsx packages/embeds/js/package.json` shows 0.10.0's direct unsafe href changed to `sanitizeUrl(...)` while the package version becomes 0.10.1; js-v0.10.1 points directly to 2c3fc7267a5e1529ba4b1a2ab4f1edb3e3b8990b. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2c3fc7 v3.15.2` fails and the same check against v3.16.0 succeeds, matching the first-party application boundary. `git show 2c3fc7` directly adds an http/https/mailto/tel allowlist sanitizer and applies it to text-bubble, image, and toast href sinks.
reasoning: The vulnerability is a stored-XSS lifecycle, not merely the final PlateBlock spelling. Authoring already allowed rich-text links, and the v2 JavaScript viewer first exposed the unsafe stored data in 3487850 by injecting serialized HTML without scheme validation. That exact member commit is smaller and causally prior to the recreated mainline PR carrier. e0a9824 removed redundant html/plainText storage and rewrote rendering to use richText nodes, but its direct href retained the same trust-boundary failure; 765c4b2 later retained it again. Therefore neither refactor is the BIC. Direct inspection of 3487850's parent tree proves the new viewer sink absent, while tree identity with 1a3869 proves how the decomposed member landed. The landed tree precedes the first js-v0.0.1 tag and remains vulnerable through js-v0.10.0. Fix 2c3fc7 applies protocol allowlisting, is exactly js-v0.10.1, and is included in v3.16.0 but not v3.15.2. Finally, attribution is based only on the decomposed BIC commit object: it is authored and committed by Baptiste Arnaud and contains no AI marker. Any AI signal on the later fix cannot attribute the 2022 root cause, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
